Subject: Dedicated capacity performance validation: latency & throughput SLOs (post-call)

Hi Joe / Sara,

Thanks for the time earlier — good discussion. As promised, here's a short recap of the performance / SLO items we agreed to validate for Acme's dedicated capacity proof-of-work (PoW), plus next steps so we can scope the bench and reserved throughput.

Key SLOs / requirements (from call)
- Latency: target 95th percentile generation latency <= 120 ms for 1k-token streaming responses (p95) for the primary model variant.
- Throughput: sustained 180 req/s for concurrent inference at peak.
- Concurrency: up to 60 concurrent active sessions (streaming enabled).
- Streaming: chunked token streaming (server-sent events / streaming socket) with <50 ms token inter-arrival on average.
- Response stability: 99.9% success rate (no OOMs / retries) during 2 hour peak window.

Questions we need answered to size the PoW correctly
1) Typical request shape: avg prompt length, avg output length (tokens). If you can share a small sample (anonymized) that would be perfect.
2) Target model(s): are you planning to run an LLaMA-2-70B style model or a smaller ~13B variant in production?
3) Preferred GPU family: do you have a preference (NVIDIA A100 / H100 / T4) for the PoW? We can run comparative benchmarks if needed.
4) Acceptable fallback behavior: if the dedicated pool is saturated, should we route to hosted capacity or queue / reject?

Proposed PoW scope & deliverables- Run comparative benchmarks across up to two GPU types (we recommend H100 and A100 for cost/perf baselines).
- Validate p95 latency and sustained throughput with your sample prompts and a simulated concurrency profile.
- Produce a sizing recommendation (reserved throughput slots), estimated GPU count, and suggested batch/kv-cache settings.
- Document streaming latency characteristics and recommended runtime settings.

Attachments: I'm attaching our short Redwood Dedicated perf playbook and a sample request spec.

Next steps
- Can you share a small sample (10-20) anonymized prompts and expected output lengths? (Sara mentioned she could provide these)
- We'll schedule a 2-hour PoW window next week (prefer Tue/Wed AM pacific) to run the tests with your SRE on-call.
- Aditya (cc'd) will follow up with specific test plan items and GPU comparison matrix.

Thanks — I'll loop in a calendar invite once we confirm times.

Best,

Thanks — adding a few technical notes and what we'll measure in the PoW: 

Bench plan / what we'll measure- End-to-end p95 generation latency for full response (streaming): measure p95 for last token and also token inter-arrival distribution.
- Sustained throughput: measure steady-state requests per second across 30 minute windows.
- Concurrency: validate with 60 simultaneous streaming sessions.
- Resource metrics: GPU utilization, memory footprint, kernel-level stalls, OOMs.
- Failure modes: tail latency and retry rates under injected interference (noisy neighbors).

GPU comparison notes (high-level)- H100: best raw throughput and lower latency on large attention workloads; higher unit cost; typically needs fewer cards for same throughput.
- A100: mature, good throughput for 13B quantized models, slightly higher latency than H100 for very large context and very long outputs, better price-performance in some clouds.
- T4 / L4: cost-effective for smaller models / lower concurrency; not ideal for heavy 800-1k token streaming at high concurrency.

Sizing estimate (very rough) for 13B quantized model- H100: ~4 GPUs to reach sustained 180 req/s with 60 concurrent streaming sessions (depends on batch settings).
- A100: ~6 GPUs for comparable steady-state throughput in our bench runs.

We'll run both variants if you want — we can also provide a CSV with per-GPU throughput estimates and per-token latency curves. For the PoW we'll need:
- The anonymized 10-20 sample prompts + expected output sizes (Joe mentioned EOD).
- A target test window and an on-call SRE/account contact for coordination.
- Any network constraints (e.g., must originate from your VPC or allowed IP ranges).

I'll prepare a short matrix (A100 vs H100) and include recommended reserved throughput (slots) and recommended autoscale headroom.
